origin.description: The size of an object, wrapped in brackets. obj_sum calls this. The result is always one string, and it may be empty.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object to summarise. Methods are in place for atomic vectors and the usual variants.

origin.details: A vector is an opening bracket, dim_desc of the object, and a closing bracket. The default method returns an empty string when the object is not a vector, which is how a function omits its size. A length-one vector is still a vector, so 1 is [1]. trees is [31 × 3] and Titanic is [4 × 2 × 2 × 2].

translation.description: The same brackets. An empty string is only for a non-vector. A length-one number is still [1].

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector, Matrix, DataFrame, Table, or any other object. trees is a DataFrame with 31 rows and 3 columns. Titanic is Table((4, 2, 2, 2)).

translation.details: vec_is false returns "". Otherwise the text is "[" + dim_desc(x) + "]". The times sign follows cli.unicode, so Titanic is [4 × 2 × 2 × 2] when unicode is true.
translation.example:
from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.unicode": True})

from pillar._vec import DataFrame, Table
from pillar.summary import size_sum

trees = DataFrame({
    "Girth": list(range(31)),
    "Height": list(range(31)),
    "Volume": list(range(31)),
})
print(size_sum(list(range(1, 11))))
print(size_sum(trees))
print(size_sum(Table((4, 2, 2, 2))))
